title: After Desvigne: Kid Rena, Punch and sitting in with Jim Robinson
summary: Nelson plays with Kid Rena and Punch, and describes resting Jim Robinson at jetty dances.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: So after Sidney Desvene and Brand broke up, then I had to just come back to this Dick's land. I knew the chords, and the punch, you know, the chords is all the same. I knew all the pieces, because I heard them play it. I used to play it then. I played with Kid Renier. Played with Punch. I didn't play with Buddy Petit, because I was old enough, but at the time he was here, and I was in the country. I could have played with him. I used to go play with Jim Robinson. He was playing with a band at the Levita. That was a jetty dance.
I used to rest him up. No, yeah.

Just rest him up. Give him a break, because they played from eight until. Peace continues. As soon as one stopped, they didn't speak of another piece. You know, so those men get rid of the tickets. You buy tickets to jetty dance.
People must love to play then. Yes. To do all that sitting in and rest people up, you know.
